metadata.title: Myles Price - Two catches in loss
metadata.description: Price caught both of his targets for 26 yards and collected 94 kick return yards and 19 punt return yards in the Vikings' 35-10 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Price played 10 offensive snaps and 10 special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver was targeted on 20 percent of his reps, making the most of his offensive opportunities as the No. 5 option. Price continues to show out on special teams, with 912 kick return yards and 281 punt return yards over 10 games so far in 2026.

metadata.title: Myles Price has Intriguing Deep-League Appeal
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Myles Price has been seeing an expanded role in the offense in recent weeks. In Week 10, Price hauled in all four of his targets for 49 yards and scored a touchdown. He quickly became a popular waiver wire pickup, but Price disappointed fantasy managers this past weekend. Price hauled in both his targets for 26 yards in the loss to the San Francisco 49ers. It wasn't a great game from Price, but the expectation is that he'll continue having an increased role as long as Jordan Addison (thumb) is out. Fantasy managers in deep leagues who might be looking for a dart throw should consider adding Price ahead of their Week 12 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

metadata.title: Myles Price comes up with two grabs in Week 11 loss
metadata.description: Myles Price caught both of his targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
metadata.analysis: Price was a popular pickup across the fantasy landscape after coming up with four receptions, including his first career TD, in Week 10. Suffice it to say, he largely disappointed Sunday night, aside from a 22-yard gain. The second-year pro has seen extra action with Jordan Addison (thumb) sidelined, but Price really only merits fantasy consideration in deeper PPR formats.

metadata.title: Myles Price an Intriguing Waiver Add After Week 10
metadata.description: Minnesota wide receiver Myles Price put together his best performance of the season in Week 10, and he gains even more fantasy value with Jordan Addison (thumb) likely to miss extended time now. Against the Packers this past week, Price caught all four of his targets for 49 yards and a touchdown - he also gained 12 yards on a rushing attempt. He played 33 offensive snaps, which was 47.8% of the team's total, and a new season-high mark. Price has 81 yards and a score over 10 receptions and 15 targets in nine games overall, plus two rushing attempts for 14 more yards. Price's role and production could improve over the next several weeks as the Vikings' offense adjusts without Addison. The trade for Kirk Cousins boosts Price's fantasy outlook as well, and the wideout suddenly becomes a deep-league fantasy starting option, and maybe someone to add in standard leagues in a couple of weeks if the production keeps coming.

metadata.title: Myles Price finds end zone in Week 10 win
metadata.description: Myles Price hauled in each of his four targets for 49 yards and one touchdown while also rushing once for 12 yards in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers in Week 10.
metadata.analysis: Price made the most of increased targets, finishing with more than three receptions while recording a touchdown for the first time this season in the win. The wideout could be in line for increased usage with WR2 Jordan Addison fighting through injury issues ahead of a Week 11 contest against the San Francisco 49ers.

metadata.title: Myles Price - On track for increased role
metadata.description: Price is set for an increase in offensive workload with Jordan Addison (thumb) sidelined, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Price reeled in a season-high four passes for 49 yards and a score during Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. The wideout was operating in a more prominent offensive role for the second week in a row with Jauan Jennings (calf) sidelined, and fellow wide receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) was unable to play as well. Addison is now expected to undergo thumb surgery, opening the door for Price to operate in an elevated position on Minnesota's offense for the time being.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Shines with elevated snaps
metadata.description: Price caught all four targets for 49 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
metadata.analysis: With Jordan Addison (thumb) inactive, Price moved up the depth chart and played 33 of 69 offensive snaps behind Justin Jefferson (63) and Tai Felton (59) in Kirk Cousins' 2026 debut with the team. Price ended up running 22 routes on Cousins' 36 dropbacks and produced the game's first touchdown, scoring from 38 yards out in the first quarter to give Minnesota a 10-0 lead. On limited offensive playing time this season, Price has recorded 10 catches for 81 yards and the one touchdown on 15 targets. He's unlikely to be a fantasy factor moving forward.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Hauls in one of four targets Monday
metadata.description: Price caught one of his four targets for six yards in a Week 9 loss to Buffalo on Monday Night Football. He also gained 12 yards on one punt return and brought back four kickoffs for 124 yards.
metadata.analysis: Price wasn't the only Minnesota pass catcher who logged an inefficient line, as starting quarterback Carson Wentz completed just eight of 25 pass attempts. Price did make an impact in the return game by averaging 31.0 yards on his four kickoff returns. Price's role continues to be mostly centered on special teams, as he's caught just four passes for 32 yards on 11 targets through eight games.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Returns vs. Indianapolis
metadata.description: Price (head) was back on the field for the second quarter of Sunday's game against the Colts, Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
metadata.analysis: Price was being evaluated by medical staff for a possible concussion, but he's been cleared to return to Sunday's contest. He'll see most of his playing time as a returner on special teams while operating in a rotational role on offense.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Being checked for concussion
metadata.description: Price is being evaluated for a possible concussion and is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Colts.
metadata.analysis: Price appeared to sustain the injury while catching a punt in the first quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's game. Tai Felton could handle return duties on kickoffs and punts for as long as Price is out of the game.

metadata.title: Myles Price catches three passes in Week 5
metadata.description: Myles Price caught three of his four targets for 20 yards with one fumble lost in the Vikings' 23-13 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 5.
metadata.analysis: Price has struggled to make an impact for head coach Kevin O'Connell, finishing with less than 30 receiving yards in each of his four contests. The pass-catcher can remain off rosters in all formats as the Vikings enter a Week 6 bye.

metadata.title: Myles Price sees one target in Week 2
metadata.description: Myles Price failed to catch his only target in the Vikings' 9-3 win over the Chicago Bears in Week 2.
metadata.analysis: Price remains minimally involved in the Minnesota passing attack to begin the season, recording one target or less in each of the first two games. The wideout remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 3 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Returns kicks
metadata.description: Price recorded five kickoff returns for 179 yards and one punt return for 13 yards in Sunday's 39-22 win over the Packers.
metadata.analysis: The wide receiver also played on three offensive snaps but did not record a target. The second-year pro has yet to record a catch in his NFL career, but he seems to have a role as a returner.

metadata.title: Myles Price Making Push For Bigger Receiving Role?
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Myles Price logged an impressive preseason debut by catching all four of his targets for 51 yards and a touchdown on Saturday against the New York Giants. An undrafted free agent from Indiana, Price made the Vikings' 53-man roster last season and finished third in the NFL in kick return yards. The second-year pro is now competing with Tai Felton and Jeshaun Jones for a secondary receiving role in the Vikings' offense, and Price's team-best 28-yard reception and acrobatic touchdown catch on Saturday certainly helped his cause. Still firmly behind Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and Jauan Jennings, Price won't factor into most standard formats, but he's a name worth knowing in formats that score return yards and deeper dynasty leagues.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Cleared for camp
metadata.description: Price passed his conditioning test and is good to go for training camp, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: The top kickoff and punt returner for the Vikings suffered an ankle injury in late Week 17 of last season. After an offseason of healing, Price is all set to suit up for training camp to attempt to defend his spot as the team's top return specialist. Tai Felton is the 24-year-old's primary competition for the role.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Won't play Sunday
metadata.description: Price (ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Packers, Dane Mizutani of the St. Paul Pioneer Press reports.
metadata.analysis: Price didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday and is now in line to miss his first game of the season Sunday. The undrafted rookie from Indiana had a solid year while operating as the Vikings' primary return man, tallying 1,479 kick-return yards (third-most in the NFL) and 298 punt-return yards across 16 games. In his absence, expect Ty Chandler to operate as the Vikings' top return specialist in Week 18.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Sits out practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Price (ankle) was a non-participant in practice Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Price hurt his ankle Christmas Day versus Detroit and hasn't recovered enough to practice. With that in mind, it's uncertain if he'll be able to play in the Vikings' season finale against Green Bay on Sunday. Price has had just a bit role on offense this season, but he's been working as Minnesota's primary kick- and punt-returner, so he'd have to be replaced in those capacities if he can't suit up Sunday.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Won't return Thursday
metadata.description: Price (ankle) has been ruled out to return to Thursday's game against the Vikings.
metadata.analysis: Price suffered an ankle injury during the opening kickoff of Thursday's divisional matchup and will not retake the field. His next opportunity to return to action will come Sunday, Jan. 4 versus the Packers in Week 18.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Hurts ankle on opening kickoff
metadata.description: Price, who injured his ankle on the opening kickoff of Thursday's game against Detroit, is questionable to return, Andrew Kramer of the Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
metadata.analysis: With Price injured, Jalen Nailor is handling punt returns. Price collapsed while running back a kickoff and was untouched.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Racks up return yardage in win
metadata.description: Price returned six kickoffs for 143 yards in Sunday's 34-26 win over the Cowboys.
metadata.analysis: Price also took the field for a play on offense, but the depth receiver has yet to touch the ball as anything but a return man through his first 14 NFL games. While ball security (four fumbles) has been somewhat of an issue for Price, he's provided a boost to the Minnesota special teams with an average of 26.0 yards per kickoff return and 9.9 yards per punt return.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Makes impact with kick returns
metadata.description: Price returned five kickoffs for an average of 32.8 yards, including a 61-yard return, in Sunday's win at Detroit. He also had a 99-yard touchdown return called back due to a holding penalty. He had one punt return for seven yards.
metadata.analysis: Price's returns had a big impact on the victory, as it set up the Vikings with good field position early in the game. His 61-yard return was the team's longest since 2022, according to the Minnesota Star Tribune.
